chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from his father, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
One who recites Surah Al-Anfal and Surah Bara'ah every month, hypocrisy will never enter him, and he will be among the Shias of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him).

key_terms.أَمِیرِ الْمُؤْمِنِینَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali (peace be upon him)
key_terms.سُورَهَ الْأَنْفَالِ: Surah Al-Anfal (The Spoils of War), the 8th chapter of the Quran
key_terms.سُورَهَ بَرَاءَهَ: Surah Bara'ah (The Declaration of Disbelief), another name for Surah At-Tawbah (The Repentance), the 9th chapter
key_terms.شِیعَه: Shia, meaning followers or partisans, here referring to the true followers of Imam Ali
key_terms.نِفَاقٌ: Hypocrisy, specifically inner hypocrisy or insincerity in faith

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of reciting Surah Al-Anfal and Surah Bara'ah monthly?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq, this hadith links the monthly recitation of Surah Al-Anfal and Surah Bara'ah to spiritual immunity from nifaq (hypocrisy) and affiliation with the Shiah of Imam Ali (AS). This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on the interconnection between Quranic recitation and adherence to the Ahl al-Bayt, reflecting the broader theological concept that true faith is inseparable from love for the Imams.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. From the previous chain from al-Hassan from his father from Abi Basir from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
One who recites Surah Anfaal and Surah Taubah every month would never get involved in hypocrisy and would be among the Shias of Amirul Momineen (a.s.).”
